summary: Observation (A/B run FS-GG/FS.GG.Templates 40116649986, main a946a7ec, one dispatch, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure, n=1 per arm, differing runner image versions 20261023.334.3 vs 20261012.334.1 with the restriction at 1 on both): on hosted ubuntu-24.04 with kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 the unchanged literal 'unshare --user --map-root-user --net -- /usr/bin/true' fails with 'write failed /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted', directly and in a NoNewPrivileges unit; dmesg shows apparmor userns_create transitioning an unconfined process to profile unprivileged_userns, then apparmor DENIED operation=capable capname=sys_admin; a post-CLONE uid_map write returns EPERM and setgroups EACCES. With 'sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0' on the ephemeral VM the same probe passes under NNP and no AppArmor line appears. This supersedes the earlier 'cause unproved' status of D5 attempts 40047202735/40057752243 for the host cause only; those attempts remain failed original evidence. Decision (Root, FS-GG/.github#4849 comment 6385676372): the sysctl is allowed on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners only, never Home or self-hosted; it is now a reviewed hosted-only step of the held D5 receiver workflow (Templates#773), not yet exercised by a D5 dispatch. The shared 4816 retained-reference workflow needs the same step before activation. Prerequisite result only: no SDK, backend or receiver was reached, and D5/4849/4644 acceptance stays open.
title: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 blocks the D5 unshare probe through AppArmor's unprivileged-userns restriction
